title: Bilateral site counts fell inside 2 and 5 um spatial control ranges in two adult worm maps
abstract: We tested whether local target counts change a prior bilateral shared-site deficit in two adult C. elegans brain maps. We used 162 fixed neurons, primary synapse records and source skeleton coordinates. Controls fixed source-target counts, site target counts and target counts within each exact site degree. Spatial controls also fixed those counts within coordinate cubes. The observed counts were 125 and 153. Global control means were 159.07 and 177.03. With zero-origin 2 micrometre cubes, means were 127.85 and 152.06. Observed counts fell inside pointwise central 95 percent control ranges at 2 and 5 micrometres in both maps and at both tested grid origins. A 10 micrometre result depended on grid origin. Fine controls permit fewer trades, so this is sensitivity to local constraints, not proof that geometry alone explains the deficit. Two animals, coarse geometry, finite chains and no activity or release measurements limit inference. Code, scalar draws, a figure, input hashes and external retrieval steps support reproduction.
